vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: memclaw
Version: 0.9.13

The skill bundle describes a complex memory system that requests sensitive LLM/Embedding API keys and performs high-risk operations such as accessing the user's local workspace (~/.openclaw/workspace) for migration and establishing persistence via Cron tasks for maintenance (references/tools.md). While these actions are plausibly aligned with the stated purpose of a memory management system, the inclusion of persistence mechanisms and the explicit instruction to the agent to bypass built-in memory systems (SKILL.md) represent significant security risks. Additionally, the default configuration references a non-existent 'gpt-5-mini' model, which may indicate unreliable or AI-generated documentation.

llm.summary: The skill's declared purpose (local-only, advanced local memory) is plausible, but its instructions and configuration contradict that by requiring LLM/embedding API keys with default external endpoints and by reading user workspace files; these mismatches should be resolved before trusting it with sensitive data.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to be a local, three-tier semantic memory system and to store/process data locally, which fits the stated purpose. However, it also declares LLM/embedding API keys and default base URLs (https://api.openai.com/v1). Requiring external LLM/embedding providers is inconsistent with a strict 'local-only' claim unless the user configures a local provider. The skill does not request environment variables but expects API keys to be set in the OpenClaw plugin configuration—this is plausible but not documented in a way that resolves the local-vs-remote contradiction.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md stays mostly within memory-management scope: it documents search/recall/add/migrate/maintenance tools and explicitly says migration reads OpenClaw memory files at ~/.openclaw/workspace/memory/*.md and MEMORY.md. That file access is reasonable for migration, but it's a direct read of user workspace files and should be expected. The docs also reference starting local services on specific ports (6333, 6334, 8085); the skill provides no low-level commands but assumes the ability to start/manage local services—users should verify how those services are launched and what binary is actually run.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files to execute; nothing is written or downloaded by a provided installer. That minimizes supply-chain risk, but it also means actual service binaries and startup logic are external to this package and must be inspected separately.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request environment variables but does require LLM and embedding API keys stored in OpenClaw plugin configuration. Requiring two provider keys is reasonable for a memory system that uses embeddings + LLMs, but the SKILL.md's statement 'Does NOT send data to external servers (all processing is local)' directly conflicts with the documented defaults pointing to api.openai.com. If you intend strict local-only operation, the skill's configuration must be changed to use local LLM/embedding endpoints; otherwise it will send memory content to third-party services.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled, does not request elevated platform privileges, and is user-invocable. It does assume it can write to the user's local data directory and manage local services, which is normal for a local memory plugin but worth verifying in the host environment.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Before installing or enabling this skill:

- Understand the local vs. external contradiction: the doc claims local-only processing but defaults to external LLM/embedding endpoints (api.openai.com). If you need true local processing, confirm and configure local LLM/embedding endpoints.
- Treat plugin-stored API keys as sensitive: the skill expects LLM/embedding keys in OpenClaw's plugin config. Verify how OpenClaw stores and protects those secrets.
- Expect the migration step to read files under ~/.openclaw/workspace/memory/ and MEMORY.md—if those files contain sensitive data, back them up and review the migration behavior first.
- Because this package has no installer or code bundled, locate and inspect the actual service binaries or scripts (Qdrant, Cortex Memory) the plugin will launch before running them; verify their origin and integrity.
- If you require strong guarantees about data not leaving your machine, ask the developer for explicit documentation that network calls are optional or for a configuration that pins endpoints to local-only providers; otherwise assume embeddings/LLM requests will go to the configured provider.

If these issues are not satisfactorily addressed, run the plugin in an isolated environment (e.g., VM or container) or avoid installing it.
llm.findings: [none] unexpected: No regex-based scan findings were produced because this is an instruction-only skill with no code files. The absence of findings does not imply safety—review the behavior described in SKILL.md (notably network calls to embedding/LLM providers and filesystem reads).
